room.title: Project and Product Managers
room.description: How a product manager holds one product's roadmap, the sprint in flight and the people who need to hear about it on one surface — the scores, the scope, the stakeholder notes and the reasons behind each decision.

desks.title: Next-quarter roadmap — scoring the shortlist
desks.description: Nine candidate bets scored with RICE against 26 person-weeks of capacity, the customer evidence behind each one, and the decision record for the roadmap review.
desks.brief:
## Next-quarter roadmap — scoring the shortlist

**Product** Corella · rostering and timesheets for hospitality venues
**Customers** about 1,400 venues · **Roadmap review** @+5d with Marcus, sales and support
**Capacity** 26 person-weeks of new work — 4 engineers × 13 weeks, half kept back for support, bugs and the shift-swap tail

### How we're scoring
RICE = reach × impact × confidence ÷ effort. Reach is venues likely to use it in a quarter; impact runs 0.25–3; effort is person-weeks including design and QA. **The scores rank the list. They don't make the decision.**

### The proposal
- **Now (19 person-weeks):** shift-swap general release, availability from the staff app, payroll export, missed-break alerts, offline clock-in
- **Next:** pay rules engine, multi-venue roster view
- **Later / not doing:** labour-cost forecast, reporting rebuild
- 7 person-weeks left unallocated on purpose — the last two quarters ran 25–30% over estimate

### Still open
Whether the pay rules engine jumps the queue. Sales say two multi-venue groups will sign if it's on the roadmap; the evidence from everyone else is thin.

callout.title: Decision for the review: pay rules engine
callout.body: Dylan wants it Now for two multi-venue groups. It scores 70 at 50% confidence and would take 12 of our 26 weeks. Proposal: keep it Next and fund a 2-week discovery spike out of the buffer.

children.label: Swaps agreed in group chats, re-keyed
How many venues have complex rules?
Missed breaks found at audit time
Alert the manager on the day
Reporting rebuild: 3 asks in a year

blocks.p: Written before the meeting so the review is spent on the open question, not on re-reading the list. Outcomes get added on the day.

ul: Shift swaps go to general release first — the most requested feature, and the beta reaches five venues this sprint
Payroll export and missed-break alerts ship together; both change timesheets
Reporting rebuild is not doing — three requests in a year, all from one group

ol: Pay rules engine: Next with a 2-week spike, or Now in place of offline clock-in and break alerts (23 of 26 weeks)?
Do we hold the 7-week buffer, or let sales spend some of it?

blocks.p: To be filled in at the review @+5d.

notes.title: Pre-reads and lobbying
notes.body:
Who has said what before the review:

- Dylan (sales): pay rules or we lose the two groups — ask him for the actual deal size
- Grace (support): break alerts would cut the compliance tickets she escalates every week
- Ines (design): offline clock-in needs a field test in a real basement kitchen, not the office
- Marcus: wants one slide, not nine rows — the chart over the table is the slide

Send the decision record to all four @+3d.

stickies.title: Before the review
stickies.body:
1. Deal size from Dylan
2. Payroll export estimate re-checked with Joon
3. Decision record out @+3d

stickies.title: Rule
stickies.body: Scores rank the list. People make the call — and write down why.

desks.title: Sprint 14 — shift-swap beta into five venues
desks.description: A two-week sprint to get shift swaps live in five pilot venues: the backlog, who needs to hear what, the stakeholder update and the one story that could push the date.
desks.brief:
## Sprint 14 — shift-swap beta

**Sprint goal** shift swaps live for staff and managers in five pilot venues by @+6d
**Team** Joon, Farah, Luis, Kemi (engineering) · Ines (design)
**Committed** 34 points · **Done** 18 · **Left** 16

### In scope
- Staff request a swap from their shift; eligible colleagues are notified
- Managers approve or decline in one tap; roster and timesheet update together
- Venue owners can see the swap history

### Out of scope this sprint
- Swaps between venues
- Blocking swaps that push someone into overtime — warned about, not blocked

### Where it stands
The build is on track; the venues are the risk. Three of five pilot venues have signed the beta agreement and Grace trains their managers @+2d. The overtime warning is blocked on pay rules data — the same gap behind the pay rules engine on the roadmap desk.

callout.title: At risk: overtime warning (3 pts)
callout.body: Joon can't finish the overtime check without each venue's pay rules, which live in payroll settings we don't read yet. Proposal: ship the beta with a plain 'this may be overtime' flag and log the gap.

rows.story: Request a swap from the shift card
Manager approve / decline in one tap
Beta flag per venue + kill switch

children.label: What's the bar for general release?
Dylan wants a demo for two groups

blocks.p: **Goal:** shift swaps live in five pilot venues by @+6d. **Confidence:** medium — the build is on track, the venues are not there yet.

ul: Staff can request a swap and eligible colleagues are notified
Managers approve or decline in one tap
18 of 34 points complete; two more stories in review
Overtime warning is blocked on pay rules data — proposing a plain warning flag instead
Only 3 of 5 pilot venues have signed; Dylan is chasing the other two

ol: Marcus: OK to ship the beta with the plain overtime flag?
Dylan: two more signed agreements by @+2d, or we switch to the reserve venues

notes.title: Things I've promised people
notes.body:
Easy to lose between the board and the chat threads:

- Grace: beta FAQ draft before her training session @+2d
- Dylan: a 10-minute demo slot for his two groups — after the beta, not before
- Kemi: a decision on whether swap history shows declined requests
- Joon: a named contact in the payroll team for the pay rules data

None of these are tickets. All of them cost trust if they slip.
